workItem.title: Add idempotency keys to the refund API
workItem.description: Clients retry refund requests on timeout. Each retry currently creates a new refund, so a customer can be refunded twice for one transaction.
workItem.acceptanceCriteria:
- A refund request may carry an idempotency key
- Repeating a key returns the original refund and does not charge again
- A request with no key behaves as it does today

comments.author: Priya
comments.body: Keys are client-generated UUIDs — same convention as the payments endpoint.

comments.author: Tom
comments.body: What should happen if the same key arrives with a different amount?

truth.approach: Persist the client-supplied idempotency key on the refund row behind a unique index; a repeated key returns the stored refund instead of creating a second one.
ambiguities: What happens when the same idempotency key arrives with a different refund amount?
How long should an idempotency key remain valid?
